size.note: Newman's Birds gives 134 cm. The male is about 20 per cent larger than the female.

habitat: Singly, in pairs or in groups in open woodland, bushveld and semi-arid grassland.
summary: A common resident. Identified by its huge size and the crest at the rear of the head. The back and wings are light brown, the wing coverts have black-and-white markings, the neck is grey, the underparts are white and the legs are pale yellow. Sexes are alike. In courtship the male inflates the throat-pouch, splays the frontal neck feathers to show their white bases, draws the crested head back, droops the wings and deflects the tail up and forwards with the white undertail coverts splayed. The courtship call is a deep wum, wum, wum, wum, wummmmm. It walks slowly and flies reluctantly. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.
